National Democratic Congress (Grenada).lead: The National Democratic Congress, also known as the National Democratic Congress of Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique, is a social democratic and centre-left political party in Grenada. It is the governing party in Grenada, having won a majority in the 2022 general elections. The party is led by current prime minister Dickon Mitchell as of October 2021.

Dickon Mitchell.stands: Dickon Mitchell is currently the prime minister of Grenada. He leads the National Democratic Congress party. He won the last general election.
Dickon Mitchell.lead: Dickon Amiss Thomas Mitchell is a Grenadian politician and attorney serving as the prime minister of Grenada since 24 June 2022 and the leader of the National Democratic Congress since 2021. He led his party to victory in the 2022 general election.

New National Party (Grenada).lead: The New National Party, also known as NNP Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique, is a conservative political party in Grenada. It is led by Emmalin Pierre. The party is sometimes referred to as "the House", or the "Green Party" in reference to its logo.

Emmalin Pierre.stands: Emmalin Pierre wants to be the leader of the opposition in parliament. She currently leads the New National Party and has been a member of parliament since 2013.
Emmalin Pierre.lead: Emmalin Pierre is a Grenadian politician who has been the Leader of the Opposition in the House of Representatives since 2025, and leader of the New National Party since 2024. She has been a member of the house since 2013, and was appointed to the Senate in 2003.

Peter David.stands: Peter David was a writer who created stories for comic books, television shows, and movies. He was known for writing many different kinds of stories, often mixing serious topics with humor and references to popular culture.
Peter David.lead: Peter Allen David, often abbreviated PAD, was an American writer of comic books, novels, television, films, and video games. His notable comic book work includes an award-winning 12-year run on The Incredible Hulk, as well as runs on Aquaman, Young Justice, SpyBoy, Supergirl, Fallen Angel, Spider-Man, Spider-Man 2099, Captain Marvel, and X-Factor.

National People's Party (The Gambia).lead: The National People's Party is a centre-right and social conservative Gambian political party centred around the leadership of the incumbent President of the Gambia, Adama Barrow.

Adama Barrow.stands: Adama Barrow wants to make Gambia a country where everyone gets along, no matter what group they belong to. He wants Gambia to work together and improve itself.
Adama Barrow.lead: Adama Barrow is a Fulani Gambian politician and real estate developer who has served as third president of the Gambia since 2017. A member of the National People's Party, he has served as the party's president since its creation in 2019. Born in Mankamang Kunda, a village in Jimara district, Barrow attended Crab Island Secondary School and the Muslim High School, the latter on a scholarship.

United Democratic Party (The Gambia).lead: The United Democratic Party is a political party in the Gambia, founded in 1996 by 3 political parties banned by the government of Yahya Jammeh led by human rights lawyer and freedom fighter Ousainou Darboe. It is the largest opposition party in the National Assembly since 2022.

Ousainou Darboe.stands: Ousainou Darboe wants to be the leader of the United Democratic Party. He wants to be President of The Gambia, and has run for that job several times. He’s focused on human rights and has worked as a lawyer for both the government and private companies.
Ousainou Darboe.lead: Ousainou Darboe is a Gambian politician and leader of the main opposition United Democratic Party. He previously served as Vice-President of the Gambia and Minister of Women's Affairs from June 2018 to March 2019, under President Adama Barrow. He also served as President Barrow's Minister of Foreign Affairs from February 2017 to June 2018.

Bharatiya Janata Party.stands: The BJP believes in ‘Integral humanism’, which focuses on a unique Indian economic model centered around people. It also promotes ‘Hindutva’, a cultural nationalism that prioritizes Indian culture over Western influences, and supports the construction of the Ram Mandir temple.
Bharatiya Janata Party.lead: The Bharatiya Janata Party is a Hindu nationalist political party in India, sitting on the right-wing to far-right of the political spectrum; it is one of the two major Indian political parties alongside the Indian National Congress. Since 2014, it has been the ruling political party in India under the incumbent prime minister Narendra Modi.

Indian National Congress.stands: The Indian National Congress believes in a mixed economy, combining elements of both government control and private enterprise. It has historically supported policies like import substitution industrialization, where India produces goods domestically instead of importing them, and a progressive tax system to reduce inequality. More recently, the party has advocated for economic liberalization and opening up the economy to foreign investment.
Indian National Congress.lead: The Indian National Congress, also known as the Congress Party, or simply the Congress, is a big tent political party in India. It is one of the oldest parties in India. Founded on 28 December 1885, it was the first modern nationalist movement to emerge in the non-European British Empire.

Democratic Party (US).stands: The Democratic Party has historically supported ideas like protecting farmers and expanding the country’s land. More recently, it has focused on helping people through economic times, like during the Great Depression with programs called the ‘New Deal’. Currently, the party supports protecting abortion rights and has a diverse range of views on economic policies.
Democratic Party (US).lead: The Democratic Party is a liberal political party in the United States, sitting on the center to center-left of the political spectrum. Founded in 1828, it is the world's oldest active political party. Its main rival is the Republican Party, and since the 1850s, both have dominated American politics.

Republican Party (US).stands: The Republican Party started with people who wanted to stop slavery and has, at times, focused on protecting businesses and building infrastructure. More recently, it has shifted towards ideas that are considered far-right, including opposing liberal policies and expressing views that some people consider prejudiced.
Republican Party (US).lead: The Republican Party, also known as the Grand Old Party, is a right-wing populist, neo-nationalist political party in the United States, sitting on the right-wing to far-right of the political spectrum. Founded in 1854, it emerged as the main rival of the Democratic Party in the 1850s, and the two parties have dominated American politics since then.

Indonesian Democratic Party of Struggle.stands: The Indonesian Democratic Party – Struggle (PDI-P) believes in following Pancasila, which is a set of principles for Indonesia. It also aims to have a balance between national identity and modern ideas, as seen in its description as a nationalist and secular party. The party has worked to be in the legislature, and has been in power in the House of Representatives.
Indonesian Democratic Party of Struggle.lead: The Indonesian Democratic Party of Struggle is a centre to centre-left, populist-secular-nationalist political party in Indonesia. Since 2014, it has been the ruling and largest party in the House of Representatives, having won 110 seats in the latest election. The party is led by Megawati Sukarnoputri, who served as the president of Indonesia from 2001 to 2004.

Golkar.stands: Golkar historically aimed to maintain a strong national identity and dominated Indonesian politics for many years. During the New Order era, it was instrumental in passing laws and controlling elections, ensuring Suharto remained in power. More recently, the party has shifted towards supporting the Jokowi administration, though it experienced internal leadership disputes before reaching a resolution.
Golkar.lead: The Party of Functional Groups, often known by its abbreviation Golkar, is a centre to centre-right big tent secular-nationalist political party in Indonesia. Founded in 1964 as the Joint Secretariat of Functional Groups, it is the oldest extant political party in Indonesia. It first participated in national elections in 1971 as Functional Groups.

Gerindra Party.stands: The party wants to change Indonesia’s political system to be based on its culture and values, using Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution. It also wants the government to be more involved in the economy, like having more state-owned businesses and protecting Indonesian businesses from foreign competition.
Gerindra Party.lead: The Great Indonesia Movement Party, better known as the Gerindra Party, is a nationalist, right-wing populist political party in Indonesia. Since 2014, it has been the third-largest party in the House of Representatives, having won 86 seats in the latest election. It currently controls the presidency and is part of the ruling government. Gerindra is led by former army general and current president Prabowo Subianto.

NasDem Party.stands: The NasDem Party wants to create a society that is democratic, just, and sovereign for Indonesia. It focuses on achieving national independence, economic independence, and protecting Indonesia’s culture, and aims to restore the original ideals of the Indonesian Republic.
NasDem Party.lead: The NasDem Party, or the National Democratic Party is an Indonesian political party. Centre-left and progressive, this party carries the theme of change and restoration of the Indonesian nation. It is partly funded by media baron Surya Paloh who founded the similarly named organization, Nasional Demokrat. Despite this, and logo similarity, Nasional Demokrat has insisted that it is not linked with the party.

National Awakening Party.stands: The Partai Kebangkitan Bangsa party believes in promoting inclusive and nationalist principles, based on Indonesia’s Pancasila doctrine. It focuses on policies like strengthening democracy in villages, protecting farmers and fishermen, and developing disadvantaged regions. The party also wants to improve the situation for laborers and increase women’s involvement in important jobs.
National Awakening Party.lead: The National Awakening Party, is an centrist Islam-based political party in Indonesia. It is also the party of the former Vice President of Indonesia, Ma'ruf Amin, who was elected to its Shura Council. The party was founded in 1999 by the traditionalist strand of Muslim society in Indonesia, which overlaps with the membership of Nahdlatul Ulama.

Prosperous Justice Party (2020).stands: The party wants to create a society that is fair, wealthy, and respected. It aims to change the way the government, courts, and military work to make democracy stronger. The party also wants to help people by reducing poverty, creating jobs, and making sure everyone has a good education.
Prosperous Justice Party (2020).lead: The Prosperous Justice Party, frequently abbreviated to PKS, and formerly the Justice Party, is an Islamist political party in Indonesia. PKS is a metamorphosis from the Justice Party established in 1998.

Pakistan Muslim League (N).stands: This party believes in a system where businesses and individuals can do well, and they want the government to let businesses work more freely. They also think it’s important to be careful with money and not spend too much.
Pakistan Muslim League (N).lead: The Pakistan Muslim League – Nawaz is a centrist political party in Pakistan. It is one of the three major mainstream political parties alongside the Pakistan People's Party and the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf. PML–N currently holds the most seats in the National Assembly; and third-most in the Senate.

Liberal Party (Brazil).stands: The Liberal Party believes in economic freedom and supporting businesses, especially in agriculture. They also want to strengthen the military and promote traditional values like family and faith. The party has recently focused on policies that align with the ideas of Jair Bolsonaro, including reducing the age at which someone can be held responsible for a crime and defending the right to own guns.
Liberal Party (Brazil).lead: The Liberal Party is a right-wing to far-right Bolsonarist political party in Brazil. From its foundation in 2006 until 2019, it was called the Party of the Republic.

Brazil of Hope.lead: The Brazil of Hope Federation or FE Brasil is an electoral and parliamentary group formed by the Workers' Party, Communist Party of Brazil and Green Party on 18 April 2022 in preparation for the 2022 general election.

Progressive Union (Brazil).stands: The Progressive Union Federation is made up of two parties that started with groups that supported Brazil’s past military rule. It currently has a large number of members and will have many representatives in Congress and local government, including mayors and governors.
Progressive Union (Brazil).lead: The Progressive Union Federation is an electoral and parliamentary group formed by Brazil Union and Progressistas. The federation brings together two parties that trace their lineages to the National Renewal Alliance, a party that supported the Brazilian military dictatorship, and its successor, the Democratic Social Party. In March 2025, with a sum of both parties, the federation had 2,410,352 registered members.

Social Democratic Party (Brazil, 2011).lead: The Social Democratic Party is a political party in Brazil led by Gilberto Kassab and uniting dissidents from various political parties, especially the Democrats, Brazilian Social Democracy Party and Party of National Mobilization. The party has become a major force for centrism in Brazil and commonly unites with both left-wing and right-wing parties.

Republicans (Brazil).stands: The party believes in traditional values like Christian beliefs, a traditional family structure, and protecting private property. It also supports economic policies that allow for private ownership and business activity.
Republicans (Brazil).lead: The Republicans, formerly the Brazilian Republican Party and originally formed as the Municipalist Renewal Party, is a Brazilian political party. Its electoral number, the numerical assignment for Brazilian political parties, is 10. The party is socially conservative and economically liberal, and has a strong association with the evangelical Universal Church of the Kingdom of God.

Brazilian Democratic Movement.stands: The party was originally created as a way for people who disagreed with the military government to have a voice. It has supported many different presidents and governments over time, and it currently focuses on modernizing Brazil through changes like reforming labor laws and the pension system, and considering selling some government companies. The party states it is open to all Brazilians who support democracy.
Brazilian Democratic Movement.lead: The Brazilian Democratic Movement is a Brazilian political party.

All Progressives Congress.stands: The APC aims to achieve a majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives. The party secured a majority in these legislative bodies following the 2019 presidential election and again in the 2023 general election.
All Progressives Congress.lead: The All Progressives Congress is one of the major contemporary political parties in Nigeria, along with the African Democratic Congress, Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peoples Democratic Party. Founded on 6 February 2013 through the merger of three major opposition parties, the party came to power following the victory of party candidate Muhammadu Buhari in the 2015 presidential election.

Peoples Democratic Party (Nigeria).stands: The Peoples Democratic Party believes in economic policies that are similar to neoliberalism, which focuses on free markets and private enterprise. They also hold conservative views on some social issues, like same-sex relations.
Peoples Democratic Party (Nigeria).lead: The Peoples Democratic Party is one of the two major contemporary political parties in Nigeria, along with its main rival, the All Progressives Congress. Its policies generally lie towards the center-right of the political spectrum. It won every presidential election between 1999 and 2011.

Labour Party (Nigeria).lead: The Labour Party is a social democratic political party in Nigeria. The party was created in 2002 and was previously known as the Party for Social Democracy before changing to its current name the following year. Built on the ideology of social democracy, the party aims to promote and defend social democratic principles and ideals for the purpose of achieving social justice, progress and unity.

United Russia.stands: United Russia aims to combine state control with market freedoms in the economy, with the goal of reducing inequality and helping those who are less fortunate. The party emphasizes a traditional, conservative approach to social and cultural issues, valuing human life and upholding constitutional rights. The party describes itself as upholding Russia’s historical traditions of statehood, both from the tsarist and Soviet eras.
United Russia.lead: The All-Russian Political Party "United Russia" is the ruling political party of Russia since 2001. As the largest party in the Russian Federation, it holds 349 of the 450 seats in the State Duma as of 2026, having constituted the majority in the chamber since 2007. Its nationalist and Eurosceptic ideology is inconsistent and embraces specific officials, all of whom support Vladimir Putin.

Communist Party of the Russian Federatio.stands: The Communist Party of the Russian Federation wants to change Russia into a new kind of socialism, similar to what China is doing. They want to bring back control of important industries like natural resources, farms, and big companies, while still letting small businesses continue to operate. They also want to increase benefits for people and protect workers' rights.
Communist Party of the Russian Federatio.lead: The Communist Party of the Russian Federation is a left-conservative, Soviet patriotic and Marxist–Leninist political party in Russia. It is the second-largest political party in Russia after United Russia. The youth organisation of the party is the Leninist Young Communist League. The CPRF can trace its origin to the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party established in March 1898.

Liberal Democratic Party of Russia.stands: The party wants Russia to become a powerful country again. It believes in a mix of private businesses and a strong government controlling the economy, and it wants Russia to have its old borders, including parts of Ukraine, Belarus, and Central Asia. The party also thinks the United States and NATO are dangerous and wants to avoid the expansion of the European Union.
Liberal Democratic Party of Russia.lead: LDPR – Liberal Democratic Party of Russia is a Russian ultranationalist and right-wing populist political party. It succeeded the Liberal Democratic Party of the Soviet Union in Russia after the dissolution of the Soviet Union. The party was led by Vladimir Zhirinovsky since its inception until his death in April 2022.

New People (political party).stands: The party wants to change how the government works, focusing on helping ordinary citizens instead of officials. They also want to improve things like roads, schools, and healthcare, and they propose changes to how the police and government work, such as increasing police salaries and reducing the number of government officials.
New People (political party).lead: New People is a populist and communitarianist political party in Russia formed in 2020. It considers itself as a "liberal party" while observers often refer to it as centre-right or also centrist. The party, like other new parties that appeared at the beginning of 2020, is accused of spoiling, justifying this opinion by the fact of quick registration and the absence of obstacles from the authorities.

A Just Russia.lead: A Just Russia is a socially conservative and left-wing nationalist political party in Russia which considers itself "democratic socialist" and social-democratic. The party is considered to be part of the "systemic opposition" and is generally sympathetic to the agenda of incumbent president Vladimir Putin, including his foreign policy.

Morena (political party).stands: Morena wants to change the way the economy works, moving away from what it sees as the problems of past economic policies. It wants to increase government spending on things like building roads and schools, and control important industries like energy and oil. It also wants to make sure everyone gets a fair wage and supports Indigenous communities.
Morena (political party).lead: The National Regeneration Movement, commonly referred to by its syllabic abbreviation Morena, is a centre-left to left-wing political party in Mexico. Founded in 2011 by Andrés Manuel López Obrador as a civil association and registered as a political party in 2014, it emerged from López Obrador's break with the Party of the Democratic Revolution.

Ecologist Green Party of Mexico.stands: The party wants to create special economic zones and shift to a different kind of government called a semi-presidential system. It also supports allowing people to work from home and has previously supported ideas like allowing abortion and same-sex marriage.
Ecologist Green Party of Mexico.lead: The Ecologist Green Party of Mexico, also known as the Green Party, is a green political party in Mexico. Founded in 1986, the party is associated with Jorge González Torres and his son Jorge Emilio González Martínez. It has seldom received more than 10% of the vote nationwide, but in the 21st century has joined alliances with different major parties.

National Action Party (Mexico).stands: The National Action Party started as a party focused on being a good, independent voice of criticism against the main party. Later, it changed and started winning local and state elections, especially in northern Mexico. It also wanted to make sure elections were fair and honest, and it supported the idea of a strong government and laws.
National Action Party (Mexico).lead: The National Action Party is a conservative political party in Mexico founded in 1939. It is one of the main political parties in the country, and, since the 1980s, has had success winning local, state, and national elections.

Labor Party (Mexico).lead: The Labor Party is a socialist political party in Mexico. It was founded on 8 December 1990. The party is currently led by Alberto Anaya. Following the 2018 election, the PT became the third-largest political party in the Chamber of Deputies with 61 deputies, after Morena with 191 and the PAN with 81.

Institutional Revolutionary Party.stands: The PRI wanted to create a system where the leaders of the Mexican Revolution could work together to solve problems after a president was killed. Later, the party aimed for a system where the president was at the top of the government, and people joined the party to get into government jobs.
Institutional Revolutionary Party.lead: The Institutional Revolutionary Party is a political party in Mexico that was founded in 1929 as the National Revolutionary Party. It became the Party of the Mexican Revolution in 1938 and the PRI in 1946. The party held uninterrupted power in the country for 71 years, from 1929 to 2000.

Citizens' Movement (Mexico).lead: Citizens' Movement, also known as the Citizens' Movement Party, is a centre-left political party in Mexico. It was founded in 1999 under the name Convergence for Democracy, which was then shortened to Convergence in 2002 and changed to Citizens' Movement in 2011.

Liberal Democratic Party (Japan).stands: The Liberal Democratic Party wants to maintain close ties with the United States and other countries in the Indo-Pacific region. They have also historically supported policies like social security and measures to control pollution, and have been willing to increase the country’s defense spending.
Liberal Democratic Party (Japan).lead: The Liberal Democratic Party, also known as Jimintō, is a major big-tent conservative and nationalist political party in Japan. Since its foundation in 1955, the LDP has been in power almost continuously—a period known as the 1955 System—except from 1993 to 1994, and again from 2009 to 2012. Sanae Takaichi has served as president of the LDP since 4 October 2025.

Centrist Reform Alliance.stands: The Centrist Reform Alliance believes in building agreement between different ideas. They want to improve the economy by aiming for double the current per capita gross domestic product, create a new system for social security, and make society more inclusive with gender equality and equal opportunities in education. The party also wants to change how politics works, including making political funds more transparent and reforming elections.
Centrist Reform Alliance.lead: The Centrist Reform Alliance, abbreviated as Chūdō or CRA, is a centrist moderate political party in Japan. It was the main opposition party in the House of Representatives from February to September 2026, holding 49 seats. The CRA was formed in January 2026 by the merger of the Constitutional Democratic Party of Japan and Komeito in the House of Representatives to challenge the Liberal Democratic Party.

Japan Innovation Party.stands: This party wants to change how Japan is run by giving more power to local areas (called ‘Dōshūsei’). They want to make things easier for businesses by cutting down on rules and regulations, and they also want to change the constitution, including making free high school education a rule. They also want to give people more choices about their family names after marriage.
Japan Innovation Party.lead: The Japan Innovation Party is a political party in Japan based in Osaka, variously described as conservative, centre-right, right-wing, and right-wing populist. The party was founded in October 2015, as Initiatives from Osaka, from a split in the old Japan Innovation Party. It ended up becoming the third-largest opposition party in the National Diet following the 2016 House of Councillors election.

Democratic Party For the People.stands: This party wants to increase the money people take home and fight against rising prices. They also want to use more government spending to help people, like spending more money on things to make people’s paychecks bigger.
Democratic Party For the People.lead: The Democratic Party For the People, also translatable as "National Democratic Party," abbreviated to DPFP or DPP, is a political party in Japan, variously described as centrist, centre-right, conservative, and populist. The first iteration of the party was formed on 7 May 2018 as a merger of the Democratic Party and Kibō no Tō.

Sanseitō.stands: The party wants to create a new constitution with minimal human rights protections. It also proposes economic policies including tax reductions and using debt, possibly including cryptocurrency, to support the economy. The party believes Japan faces threats from global elites and foreign residents, and advocates for a ‘Japanese First’ nationalist agenda.
Sanseitō.who: The party primarily attracts younger men who are new to politics and may be disillusioned with existing political systems.
Sanseitō.lead: Sanseitō is an ultraconservative, right-wing populist political party in Japan. It is on the far-right of the political spectrum. The party was founded in 2020 by Sohei Kamiya, the current secretary general of the party, and won a seat in the 2022 House of Councillors election, also becoming an official political party by winning more than 2% of the vote in the election.

Team Mirai.lead: Team Mirai is a political party in Japan founded by AI engineer Takahiro Anno. The party supports E-democracy and has been described as technocratic. The party was established on 8 May 2025, evolving from "Team Anno," which supported his candidacy in the 2024 Tokyo gubernatorial election. " In the 2025 Japanese House of Councillors election, the party won its first seat in the Diet.

Nation's Future Party.stands: The Nation's Future Party wants to support the policies of President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi. It currently holds a majority of seats in the House of Representatives and a plurality of seats in the Senate, giving it a significant role in the Egyptian government.
Nation's Future Party.lead: The Nation's Future Party, also known as the Future of a Nation Party, the Future of the Homeland Party, the Homeland's Future Party, and transliterated as Mostaqbal Watan, is an Egyptian political party. The party is often seen as a "party of power", created for the sole purpose of backing President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi and his policies.

Homeland Defenders Party.lead: The Homeland Defenders Party, also translated as Protectors of the Nation, and Guardians of the Nation, is a centrist political party in Egypt.

National Front Party (Egypt).lead: The National Front Party is an Egyptian political party founded in December 2024.

Republican People's Party (Egypt).stands: The Republican People's Party is made up of former government ministers. It is currently headed by Hazem Omar, who previously chaired the Senate foreign relations committee.
Republican People's Party (Egypt).lead: The Republican People's Party is an Egyptian political party made up of former government ministers. It is currently headed by former chairman of the Senate foreign relations committee, Hazem Omar.

Justice Party (Egypt).stands: The Justice Party was formed after the 2011 Egyptian Revolution and includes members from various groups involved in that revolution. It describes itself as a party focused on political programs, rather than a specific political idea.
Justice Party (Egypt).lead: The Justice Party is a political party in Egypt. It was founded after the Egyptian Revolution of 2011 by a group of people from different movements that led to the revolution including the April 6 Youth Movement, the National Association for Change and Kefaya.

Justice and Development Party (Turkey).lead: The Justice and Development Party, abbreviated officially as AK Party in English, is a political party in Turkey. It has been the ruling party of Turkey since 2002. Third-party sources often refer to the party as national conservative, social conservative, right-wing populist and as espousing neo-Ottomanism.

Republican People's Party.stands: The Republican People's Party wants to create a country based on ideas like protecting workers’ rights, making sure schools and universities are independent from the government, and having a system where laws are checked by a special court. It also wants to keep the country separate from religion and to make sure everyone has a voice in how the country is run.
Republican People's Party.lead: The Republican People's Party is a centre-left, social democratic and Kemalist political party in Turkey. It is the oldest political party in Turkey, founded by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the first president and founder of the modern Republic of Turkey. The party is also cited as the founding party of modern Turkey.

YSGP.lead: The Party of Greens and the Left Future, abbreviated as Green Left Party, is a green and left-libertarian party in Turkey.

Nationalist Movement Party.lead: The Nationalist Movement Party, or alternatively translated as Nationalist Action Party, is a far-right, ultranationalist political party in Turkey. The party is neo-fascist and has been linked to violent paramilitaries and organized crime groups. The party's youth wing is the Grey Wolves organization, which is also known as the "Nationalist Hearths".

Good Party.stands: The İYİ Party wants to create a new constitution and have a system where the parliament has more power. They also want to make sure the courts and other important places work fairly and honestly. The party believes in being a nationalist, developmentalist, and democratic party, and it values the ideas of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, Turkey’s founder.
Good Party.lead: The Good Party is a nationalist, Kemalist and conservative political party in Turkey, established on 25 October 2017 by Meral Akşener. According to Meral Akşener, the letters İYİ are a reference to the tamga of the Kayı tribe which also represents the party's name and flag. The party's official name is İyi Parti and official abbreviation is İYİ Parti.

New Welfare Party.stands: The New Welfare Party wants to prioritize morality and spirituality, and then reshape the world order with Turkey as a leader. They propose a new presidential system and are against trade with Israel, as well as the operation of the Kürecik Radar Station. The party also opposes LGBT rights and aims to change a law protecting women and children from domestic violence.
New Welfare Party.lead: The New Welfare Party is an Islamist and ultraconservative political party in Turkey, founded on 23 November 2018. The party positions itself as the successor to the Welfare Party, which was a prominent Islamist political party in the 1990s.

CDU/CSU.lead: CDU/CSU, unofficially the Union parties or the Union, is a centre-right Christian democratic and conservative political alliance of two political parties in Germany: the Christian Democratic Union of Germany and the Christian Social Union in Bavaria. The CSU contests elections only in Bavaria, while the CDU operates in the other 15 states of Germany.

Alternative for Germany.stands: The party wants a Germany that protects its own culture and identity, and it wants Germany to make its own decisions about things like trade with Europe. It also wants to change how Europe works and limit the number of people who come to live in Germany.
Alternative for Germany.lead: Alternative for Germany is a far-right, right-wing populist, national conservative, and in parts völkisch nationalist political party in Germany. It has 151 members of the Bundestag and 15 members of the European Parliament. It is the largest opposition party in the Bundestag and a member of the Europe of Sovereign Nations Group in the European Parliament.

Social Democratic Party of Germany.lead: The Social Democratic Party of Germany is a social democratic political party in Germany. It is one of the major parties of contemporary Germany. Lars Klingbeil has been the party's co-leader since the 2021 SPD federal Party convention and served together with Bärbel Bas from June 2025 to October 2026, when she resigned.

Alliance 90/The Greens.lead: Alliance 90/The Greens, often simply referred to as the Greens, is a green political party in Germany. It was formed in 1993 by the merger of the Greens and Alliance 90. The Greens had itself merged with the East German Green Party after German reunification in 1990. Since November 2024, Franziska Brantner and Felix Banaszak have been co-leaders of the party.

Die Linke.stands: Die Linke wants the government to spend more money on things like schools, hospitals, and building roads. They also want to make big companies pay more taxes and make sure that rich people pay a lot more taxes too. They want to reduce the number of soldiers in Germany and want Germany to work with other countries peacefully, not fight.
Die Linke.lead: Die Linke, also known as the Left Party, is a democratic socialist political party in Germany. The party was founded in 2007 as the result of the merger of the Party of Democratic Socialism and Labour and Social Justice – The Electoral Alternative. Through the PDS, the party is the direct descendant of the Marxist–Leninist ruling party of former East Germany, the Socialist Unity Party of Germany.

South Schleswig Voters' Association.stands: The South Schleswig Voters' Association wants to support the welfare state and a more free-market approach to labor than is typical in Germany. The party also represents the interests of the Danish and Frisian minorities in Schleswig-Holstein, and they secured seats in both the state parliament and the federal parliament through winning enough votes.
South Schleswig Voters' Association.lead: The South Schleswig Voters' Association is a regionalist political party in Schleswig-Holstein in northern Germany. The party represents the Danish and Frisian minorities of the state.

Brothers of Italy.lead: Brothers of Italy is a national-conservative and right-wing populist political party in Italy, that is currently the country's ruling party. After becoming the largest party in the 2022 Italian general election, it consolidated as one of the two major political parties in Italy during the 2020s, along with the Democratic Party. The party is led by Giorgia Meloni, the incumbent Prime Minister of Italy.

Five Star Movement.stands: The party wants to use the internet for direct democracy and citizen involvement in government decisions. It also wants to focus on environmental issues like creating a green economy, protecting territory, and promoting sustainable mobility. Furthermore, the party proposes changes like legalizing cannabis and euthanasia, and creating a common European army.
Five Star Movement.lead: The Five Star Movement is a political party in Italy, led by Giuseppe Conte. It was launched on 4 October 2009 by Beppe Grillo, a political activist and comedian, and Gianroberto Casaleggio, a web strategist.

Action – Italia Viva.stands: The party, Action – Italia Viva, participated in the 2022 Italian general election as a liberal and centrist group. It was named Action – Italia Viva – Renew Europe in the parliament.
Action – Italia Viva.lead: Action – Italia Viva, informally known as the Third Pole, was a liberal and centrist parliamentary group and electoral list which ran in the 2022 Italian general election. The list was led by Carlo Calenda. During the 19th legislature, it named its parliamentary group Action – Italia Viva – Renew Europe in the Chamber and the Senate.

Rebuilding Korea Party.stands: The Rebuilding Korea Party wants to change how the government uses prosecutors and make the Public Prosecutor’s Office less powerful. They also want the government to do more to help people, like expanding programs to help those who need it and investing in things like science and the environment. Finally, they want to have a friendly relationship with North Korea and work towards getting rid of weapons on the Korean Peninsula.
Rebuilding Korea Party.lead: The Rebuilding Korea Party is a South Korean political party founded by former Minister of Justice Cho Kuk ahead of the 2024 South Korean legislative election. The name of the party can be pronounced as 'Jo-guk Hyeok-sin Dang' in Korean. The word 'Jo-guk' refers to 'Fatherland', but also refers to the name of the party founder Cho Kuk, which shares the same spelling in Korean. However, the Hanja is different.

Reform Party (South Korea).lead: The Reform Party is a South Korean political party.

People's Party (Spain).stands: The People's Party wants to maintain Spain's existing system of autonomous communities and the country's monarchy. It also aims to strengthen ties with the United States and has historically opposed same-sex marriage, though some members now support it.
People's Party (Spain).lead: The People's Party known mostly by its acronym, PP, is a conservative and Christian democratic political party in Spain. The People's Party was a 1989 re-foundation of People's Alliance, a party led by former minister Manuel Fraga. It was founded in 1976 as alliance of post-Francoist proto-parties. The new party combined the conservative AP with several small Christian democratic and liberal parties.

Spanish Socialist Workers' Party.lead: The Spanish Socialist Workers' Party is a social democratic political party in Spain. The PSOE has been in government longer than any other political party in modern democratic Spain: from 1982 to 1996 under Felipe González, 2004 to 2011 under José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, and since 2018 under Pedro Sánchez. The PSOE was founded in 1879, making it the oldest party currently active in Spain.

Vox (political party).stands: Vox wants to maintain the Spanish monarchy and change how votes are counted so everyone’s vote is equal. The party also wants to change laws about remembering the past and opposes the removal of Franco’s remains.
Vox (political party).lead: Vox is a nationalist and right-wing Eurosceptic political party in Spain. Founded in 2013, it is led by party president Santiago Abascal, and vice president and secretary-general Ignacio Garriga. The party entered the Spanish parliament for the first time after winning seats in the April 2019 general election.

Sumar (electoral alliance).lead: Sumar is an electoral alliance and parliamentary group established ahead of the 2023 Spanish general election, founded by Spanish second deputy prime minister and labour minister Yolanda Díaz, provisionally registered as an association on 28 March 2022 and publicly unveiled on 18 May.

Republican Left of Catalonia.lead: The Republican Left of Catalonia, also known as the Republican Party of Catalonia, is a pro-Catalan independence, social democratic political party in the Spanish autonomous community of Catalonia, with a presence also in Valencia, the Balearic Islands and the French department of Pyrénées-Orientales.

Junts.stands: The party wants to defend the right to self-determination and enforce Catalan independence unilaterally. It also aims to bring together Catalanism with a social and economic agenda for Catalonia, while promoting democratic souverainism and direct democracy.
Junts.lead: Together for Catalonia, often shortened to Junts, is a Catalan pro-independence and populist political party that sits on the centre-right of the political spectrum. It is the second-largest party in the Parliament of Catalonia, holding 35 of the 135 seats. The current party president since 2024 is Carles Puigdemont.

La Libertad Avanza.lead: La Libertad Avanza is a political coalition and party in Argentina. LLA was formed as an electoral alliance in 2021, and as a nationwide party in 2024. It has been described as conservative, social conservative, and ultraconservative on social and cultural issues, and as right-wing libertarian or ultra-liberal on economic issues.

Homeland Force.lead: The Homeland Force, also known as the Union for the Homeland until 2025, is a centre-left to left-wing political and electoral coalition of Peronist political parties in Argentina. It has been the main opposition coalition since December 2023.

United Provinces (political coalition).lead: United Provinces is a political coalition in Argentina created to compete in the 2025 legislative election. It comprises the provincial governors of Córdoba, Santa Fe, Corrientes, Jujuy, Chubut and Santa Cruz.

Workers' Left Front.lead: The Workers' Left Front – Unity is an electoral alliance of four Trotskyist parties in Argentina: the Workers' Party, the Socialist Workers' Party, Socialist Left, and the Workers' Socialist Movement. Initially founded in 2011, the alliance added MST in 2019.

Conservative.stands: This party generally wants to maintain existing social structures and customs, such as the family, religion, and the nation-state. They often emphasize things like property rights, the rule of law, and a respect for established hierarchies, like those found in a monarchy or aristocracy.
Conservative.lead: Conservatism is a cultural, social, and political philosophy and ideology that seeks to promote and preserve traditional institutions, customs, and values. The central tenets of conservatism may vary in relation to the culture and civilization in which it appears.

Green.lead: Green is the color between cyan and yellow on the visible spectrum. It has 295–350 different shades. It is evoked by light which has a dominant wavelength of roughly 495–570 nm.

Australian Labor Party.stands: The Australian Labor Party believes in a system where industries are managed in a way that benefits everyone, aiming to reduce exploitation and unfair practices. They also want to maintain a private sector alongside this, and allow people to own private property. Historically, the party has aimed for a world where production is for use, not for making money.
Australian Labor Party.lead: The Australian Labor Party is the major social democratic political party in Australia. Sitting on the centre-left of the political spectrum, it is the oldest active party in the country, having been founded in 1891. It is one of the two major parties in Australian politics, its main rival being the Liberal–National Coalition.

Liberal–National Coalition.stands: The Coalition wants to reduce the number of new people moving to Australia each year, aiming for 140,000 permanent migrants. It also wants to focus on national security and counter-terrorism, including creating a taskforce to address antisemitism.
Liberal–National Coalition.who: The Coalition primarily draws support from men, middle-class people earning between A$45,001 and A$80,000 per year, and homeowners. It has significant support in rural and regional areas, particularly in Queensland, and some areas of major cities like Sydney and Melbourne.
Liberal–National Coalition.lead: The Liberal–National Coalition, commonly known as the Coalition or the LNP, is an alliance of liberal conservative and centre-right political parties in Australia. Its primary members are the Liberal Party of Australia and the National Party of Australia. It is one of the two major groupings in Australian politics, and its main rival is the Australian Labor Party.

Independent politicians in Australia.lead: An independent politician is a person who has served in a political office while not affiliated to any political party. Many of these have either resigned or been expelled from membership in political parties, and some have gone on to form their own political parties over time. In some cases members of parliament sit as an independent while still holding party leadership.

Australian Greens.lead: The Australian Greens, commonly referred to simply as the Greens, are a left-wing green Australian political party. As of 2025, the Greens are the third-largest political party in Australia by vote and the fourth-largest by elected representation. The party was formed in 1992 as a confederation of eight state and territorial parties.

Katter's Australian Party.stands: The party wants to protect farming and businesses in North Queensland by using tariffs and other trade barriers. They also believe in helping people who need support, and want to make North Queensland a separate state. The party also wants to keep things like farming and local businesses strong.
Katter's Australian Party.lead: Katter's Australian Party is an agrarian populist political party in Australia that advocates for agrarian socialist economic policies and conservative social policies. It was founded by politician Bob Katter, an independent and former Nationals MP for the seat of Kennedy, with a registration application lodged to the Australian Electoral Commission in 2011.

Centre Alliance.stands: Centre Alliance wants to support things like same-sex marriage and legalising euthanasia. They also want to encourage making things in Australia, like defence equipment, and they believe in changing how Australia’s intelligence agencies work. The party also supports changes to university fees, aiming to increase places and lower costs in certain fields.
Centre Alliance.lead: Centre Alliance, formerly known as the Nick Xenophon Team, is a centrist and social liberal Australian political party based in the state of South Australia.

Dhekelia Cantonment.lead: Dhekelia Cantonment, also simply named Dhekelia, is a military base in Akrotiri and Dhekelia, a British Overseas Territory on the island of Cyprus, administered as the Sovereign Base Areas. It is the larger of the two British military bases on the island, and it is also the location of Alexander Barracks, which is home to the 2nd Battalion, The Princess of Wales's Royal Regiment.

Politics of Saint Martin.lead: The Collectivity of Saint Martin was a French commune for many years and formed part of Guadeloupe, which is an overseas région and département of France and is therefore in the European Union. In 2003, the population of the French part of the island voted in favour of secession from Guadeloupe in order to form a separate overseas collectivity of France.

Elections in Saint Martin.lead: The Collectivity of Saint Martin was a French commune for many years and formed part of Guadeloupe, which is an overseas région and département of France and is therefore in the European Union. In 2003, the population of the French part of the island voted in favour of secession from Guadeloupe in order to form a separate overseas collectivity of France.

History of Saint Martin.lead: St. Martin's history shares many commonalities with other Caribbean islands. Its earliest inhabitants were Amerindians, followed by Europeans who brought slavery to exploit commercial interests.

Sint Maarten.lead: Sint Maarten, officially the Country of Sint Maarten, is a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands located in the Caribbean region of North America. With a population of 58,477 as of June 2023 on an area of 34 km2, it encompasses the southern 44% of the divided island of Saint Martin, while the northern 56% of the island constitutes the French overseas collectivity of Saint Martin.

Politics of Sint Maarten.lead: Sint Maarten, a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, has a government formed by the monarch, represented by the governor, and the ministers. The Prime Minister of Sint Maarten presides over the council of ministers. Executive power is exercised by the government. Legislative power is vested in both the government and parliament.

Elections in Sint Maarten.lead: Sint Maarten elects a legislature called the Estates of Sint Maarten. As the country has no devolved government, this is the only chosen representation of the island. It consists of 15 members, elected for a four-year term by proportional representation.

History of Sint Maarten.lead: Sint Maarten, officially the Country of Sint Maarten, is a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands located in the Caribbean region of North America. With a population of 58,477 as of June 2023 on an area of 34 km2, it encompasses the southern 44% of the divided island of Saint Martin, while the northern 56% of the island constitutes the French overseas collectivity of Saint Martin.

Guantanamo Bay Naval Base.lead: Guantanamo Bay Naval Base, officially known as Naval Station Guantanamo Bay or NSGB, is a United States military base located on 45 square miles of land and water on the shore of Guantánamo Bay at the southeastern end of Cuba. S. since 1903 as a coaling station and naval base. It is the oldest overseas American naval base. S.

Brazilian Island.lead: Brazilian Island is a small uninhabited river island at the confluence of the Uruguay River and the Quaraí River, between the borders of Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay, which is disputed by the two latter countries. 9 km wide, and it is located at 30°10′56″S 57°37′43″W.

Gibraltar.lead: Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory and city located near the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula, on the Bay of Gibraltar, near the exit of the Mediterranean Sea into the Atlantic Ocean. 8 km2 and is bordered to the north by Spain. The landscape is dominated by the Rock of Gibraltar, at the foot of which is a densely populated town area. Gibraltar is home to around 38,000 people, primarily Gibraltarians.

Politics of Gibraltar.lead: The politics of Gibraltar takes place within a framework of a parliamentary representative democratic British Overseas Territory, whereby the Monarch of the United Kingdom is the constitutional head of state represented by the Governor of Gibraltar. The Chief Minister of Gibraltar is the head of Government.

Elections in Gibraltar.lead: Under the Gibraltar Constitution Order 2006 and the Parliament Act 1950, Gibraltar elects the 17 Members of Parliament who make up its legislature, the Gibraltar Parliament. Members serve a four-year term and are elected from a single constituency under the limited voting system, in which each voter may cast up to ten votes.

History of Gibraltar.lead: The history of Gibraltar, a small peninsula on the southern Iberian coast near the entrance of the Mediterranean Sea, spans over 2,900 years. The peninsula was a place of reverence in ancient times, and it later became "one of the most densely fortified and fought-over places in Europe". Gibraltar's location has given it an outsized role in the history of Europe.

Hong Kong.lead: Hong Kong is a special administrative region of China. Situated on China's southern coast just south of Shenzhen, it consists of Hong Kong Island, Kowloon, and the New Territories. 5 million residents in a 1,114-square-kilometre territory, Hong Kong is the fourth-most densely populated region in the world.

Politics of Hong Kong.lead: The politics of Hong Kong takes place in a framework of a political system dominated by its quasi-constitutional document, the Hong Kong Basic Law, its own legislature, the Chief Executive as the head of government and of the Special Administrative Region and of a politically constrained multi-party executive-led system.

Elections in Hong Kong.lead: Elections in Hong Kong take place when certain political offices in the government need to be filled. Hong Kong has a multi-party system, with numerous parties in the Legislative Council. The Chief Executive of Hong Kong is nonpartisan. Every four years, ninety representatives are chosen to sit on the unicameral Legislative Council of Hong Kong.

History of Hong Kong.lead: The region of Hong Kong has been inhabited since the Old Stone Age, later becoming part of the Chinese Empire with its loose incorporation into the Qin dynasty. Starting out as a farming fishing village and salt production site, it became an important free port and eventually a major international financial center.

United Nations Buffer Zone in Cyprus.lead: The United Nations Buffer Zone in Cyprus is a former demilitarized zone, patrolled by the United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus, that was established between 1964 and 1990.

Siachen Glacier.lead: The Siachen Glacier is a glacier located in the eastern Karakoram range of the Himalayas, in Indian-administered Ladakh. It is situated just northeast of the terminal point NJ9842 of the Line of Control between India and Pakistan, and to the south of the Line of Actual Control between India and China, in the disputed Kashmir region.

Baikonur.lead: Baikonur is a city in Kazakhstan on the northern bank of the Syr Darya river. It is currently leased and administered by the Russian Federation until 2050. It was constructed to serve the Baikonur Cosmodrome with administrative offices and employee housing. During the Soviet period, the town was known as Leninsk, and was sometimes referred to as Zvezdograd.

History of Baikonur.lead: Baikonur is a city in Kazakhstan on the northern bank of the Syr Darya river. It is currently leased and administered by the Russian Federation until 2050. It was constructed to serve the Baikonur Cosmodrome with administrative offices and employee housing. During the Soviet period, the town was known as Leninsk, and was sometimes referred to as Zvezdograd.

Southern Patagonian Ice Field.lead: The Southern Patagonian Ice Field, located at the Southern Patagonic Andes between Chile and Argentina, is the world's second largest contiguous extrapolar ice field. It is the bigger of two remnant parts of the Patagonian Ice Sheet, which covered all of southern Chile during the last glacial period, locally called the Llanquihue glaciation.

Bir Tawil.lead: Bir Tawil is a 2,060 km2 area of land along the border between Egypt and Sudan which is claimed by neither country. Together with the neighbouring Halaib Triangle, it is sometimes called the Bir Tawil Triangle, despite its quadrilateral shape; the two regions border at a quadripoint.

Antarctica.lead: Antarctica is Earth's southernmost and least-populated continent. Situated almost entirely south of the Antarctic Circle and surrounded by the Southern Ocean, it contains the geographic South Pole. Antarctica is the fifth-largest continent, being about 40% larger than Europe, and has an area of 14,200,000 km2. 9 km.

Politics of Antarctica.lead: Antarctica is Earth's southernmost and least-populated continent. Situated almost entirely south of the Antarctic Circle and surrounded by the Southern Ocean, it contains the geographic South Pole. Antarctica is the fifth-largest continent, being about 40% larger than Europe, and has an area of 14,200,000 km2. 9 km.

Elections in Antarctica.lead: Elections in Antarctica are held by countries which have set up research stations in the continent, allowing their staff to vote while stationed outside their home countries. Since Antarctica has no permanent population nor a locally elected government, these elections are held under overseas electoral precincts which allow non-resident citizen voting.

History of Antarctica.lead: The history of Antarctica emerges from early Western theories of a vast continent, known as Terra Australis, believed to exist in the far south of the globe. The term Antarctic, referring to the opposite of the Arctic Circle, was coined by Marinus of Tyre in the 2nd century AD.

Curaçao.lead: Curaçao, officially the Country of Curaçao, is a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. It is an island country located in the southern Caribbean Sea, specifically the Dutch Caribbean region, about 65 km north of Venezuela and 80 km southeast of Aruba. Curaçao includes the main island of Curaçao, and the much smaller, uninhabited island of Klein Curaçao.

Politics of Curaçao.lead: Curaçao, officially the Country of Curaçao, is a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. It is an island country located in the southern Caribbean Sea, specifically the Dutch Caribbean region, about 65 km north of Venezuela and 80 km southeast of Aruba. Curaçao includes the main island of Curaçao, and the much smaller, uninhabited island of Klein Curaçao.

Elections in Curaçao.lead: Curaçao elects a legislature called the Estates of Curaçao. It consists of 21 members, elected for a four-year term by proportional representation. The first Estates of Curaçao were the succession of the Island council of Curaçao, upon the dissolution of the Netherlands Antilles in 2010. In October 2012, elections were held for the Estates.

History of Curaçao.lead: The history of Curaçao starts with settlement by the Arawakan-speaking Indigenous people who migrated from the South American mainland. They are believed to have inhabited the island for many hundreds of years before the arrival of Europeans.

Aruba.lead: Aruba, officially the Country of Aruba, is an island constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, in the southern Caribbean Sea 29 kilometres north of the Venezuelan peninsula of Paraguaná and 80 kilometres north-west of Curaçao. In 1986, Aruba became a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands and acquired the official name.

Politics of Aruba.lead: Aruba is a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands and a parliamentary representative democracy, whereby the governor in his capacity as the King's representative is the de jure head of government and of a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the government. Legislative power is vested in both the government and the Parliament.

Elections in Aruba.lead: Aruba elects a legislature on the national level. The Estates have 21 members, elected for a four-year term by Open list Party-list proportional representation. Seats are distributed between parties that have gained at least one full quota using the Hagenbach-Bischoff system.

History of Aruba.lead: Aruba, officially the Country of Aruba, is an island constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, in the southern Caribbean Sea 29 kilometres north of the Venezuelan peninsula of Paraguaná and 80 kilometres north-west of Curaçao. In 1986, Aruba became a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands and acquired the official name.

Turks and Caicos Islands.lead: Turks and Caicos Islands is a British Overseas Territory consisting of the larger Caicos Islands and smaller Turks Islands, two groups of tropical islands in the Lucayan Archipelago of the Atlantic Ocean and northern West Indies. They are known primarily for tourism and as an offshore financial centre.

Saint Pierre and Miquelon.lead: Saint Pierre and Miquelon, officially the Territorial Collectivity of Saint Pierre and Miquelon, is a self-governing territorial overseas collectivity of France in the northwestern Atlantic Ocean, located off the Canadian island of Newfoundland. Saint Pierre and Miquelon is an archipelago of eight islands, covering 242 km2 of land.

Politics of Saint Pierre and Miquelon.lead: The politics of Saint Pierre and Miquelon take place in the framework of a parliamentary representative democratic French overseas collectivity, whereby the President of the Territorial Council is the head of government, and of a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the government, the « Conseil exécutif ».

Elections in Saint Pierre and Miquelon.lead: Elections are held in Saint-Pierre and Miquelon for the French president, a member of the National Assembly, a member of the Senate, and a territorial legislature.

History of Saint Pierre and Miquelon.lead: The history of Saint Pierre and Miquelon is one of early settlement by Europeans taking advantage of the rich fishing grounds near Saint-Pierre and Miquelon, and is characterized by periods of conflict between the French and British. There is evidence of prehistoric native inhabitants on the islands, but there is no record of native inhabitants at the time of European exploration.

Pitcairn Islands.lead: The Pitcairn Islands, officially Pitcairn, Henderson, Ducie and Oeno Islands, are a group of four volcanic islands in the southern Pacific Ocean that form the sole British Overseas Territory in the Pacific Ocean. The four islands—Pitcairn, Henderson, Ducie and Oeno—are scattered across several hundred kilometres of ocean and have a combined land area of about 47 square kilometres.

French Southern and Antarctic Lands.lead: The French Southern and Antarctic Lands is an overseas territory of France. It consists of: Adélie Land, the French claim on the continent of Antarctica. Crozet Islands, a group in the southern Indian Ocean, south of Madagascar. Kerguelen Islands, a group of volcanic islands in the southern Indian Ocean, southeast of Africa and southwest of Australia.

United States Minor Outlying Islands.lead: The United States Minor Outlying Islands is a statistical designation applying to the minor outlying islands and groups of islands that comprise eight United States insular areas and territories in the Pacific Ocean and one in the Caribbean Sea. It is defined by the International Organization for Standardization's ISO 3166-1 code. The entry code is ISO 3166-2:UM.

Montserrat.lead: Montserrat is a British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean. It is part of the Leeward Islands, the northern portion of the Lesser Antilles chain of the West Indies. Montserrat is about 16 km long and 11 km wide, with roughly 40 km of coastline. It is nicknamed "The Emerald Isle of the Caribbean" both for its resemblance to coastal Ireland and for the Irish ancestry of many of its inhabitants.

Politics of Montserrat.lead: Politics of Montserrat takes place in a framework of a parliamentary representative democratic dependency, whereby the Premier is the head of government, and of a multi-party system. Montserrat is an internally self-governing overseas territory of the United Kingdom. The United Nations Committee on Decolonization includes Montserrat on the United Nations list of non-self-governing territories.

Elections in Montserrat.lead: Elections in Montserrat take place within the framework of a multi-party democracy and a parliamentary system. The Legislative Assembly is directly elected, and a Chief Minister is selected by the party or coalition with the most seats in the Assembly.

History of Montserrat.lead: Montserrat is a British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean. It is part of the Leeward Islands, the northern portion of the Lesser Antilles chain of the West Indies. Montserrat is about 16 km long and 11 km wide, with roughly 40 km of coastline. It is nicknamed "The Emerald Isle of the Caribbean" both for its resemblance to coastal Ireland and for the Irish ancestry of many of its inhabitants.

United States Virgin Islands.lead: The United States Virgin Islands, officially the Virgin Islands of the United States, is a Caribbean unincorporated territory of the United States. The islands are geographically part of the Virgin Islands archipelago and are located in the Leeward Islands of the Lesser Antilles. The islands have a tropical climate. S.

Saint Barthélemy.lead: Saint Barthélemy, officially the Territorial Collectivity of Saint Barthélemy, also known as St. Barts and St. Barths or St. Barth, is an overseas collectivity of France in the Caribbean. The island lies about 30 kilometres southeast of the island of Saint Martin. It is northeast of the Dutch islands of Saba and Sint Eustatius, and north of the independent country of Saint Kitts and Nevis.

Politics of Saint Barthélemy.lead: Saint Barthélemy, officially the Territorial Collectivity of Saint Barthélemy, also known as St. Barts and St. Barths or St. Barth, is an overseas collectivity of France in the Caribbean. The island lies about 30 kilometres southeast of the island of Saint Martin. It is northeast of the Dutch islands of Saba and Sint Eustatius, and north of the independent country of Saint Kitts and Nevis.

Elections in Saint Barthélemy.lead: Saint Barthélemy, officially the Territorial Collectivity of Saint Barthélemy, also known as St. Barts and St. Barths or St. Barth, is an overseas collectivity of France in the Caribbean. The island lies about 30 kilometres southeast of the island of Saint Martin. It is northeast of the Dutch islands of Saba and Sint Eustatius, and north of the independent country of Saint Kitts and Nevis.

History of Saint Barthélemy.lead: Saint Barthélemy, officially the Territorial Collectivity of Saint Barthélemy, also known as St. Barts and St. Barths or St. Barth, is an overseas collectivity of France in the Caribbean. The island lies about 30 kilometres southeast of the island of Saint Martin. It is northeast of the Dutch islands of Saba and Sint Eustatius, and north of the independent country of Saint Kitts and Nevis.

Puerto Rico.lead: Puerto Rico, officially the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, is a self-governing Caribbean archipelago and island organized as an unincorporated territory of the United States under the designation of commonwealth. S. Virgin Islands in the Lesser Antilles, it consists of the eponymous main island and numerous smaller islands, including Vieques, Culebra, and Mona.

Politics of Puerto Rico.lead: The politics of Puerto Rico take place in the framework of a democratic republic form of government that is under the jurisdiction and sovereignty of the United States Congress as an organized unincorporated territory. Since the 1898 invasion of Puerto Rico by the United States during the Spanish–American War, politics in Puerto Rico have been significantly shaped by its status as territory of the United States.

Elections in Puerto Rico.lead: Elections in Puerto Rico are guaranteed by Article Six of the Constitution of Puerto Rico and the Electoral Code of Puerto Rico for the 21st Century Act. All processes are overseen and managed in whole by the Puerto Rico State Elections Commission; an autonomous agency of the executive branch of the government of Puerto Rico.

History of Puerto Rico.lead: The history of Puerto Rico began with the settlement of the Ortoiroid people before 430 BC. At the time of Christopher Columbus's arrival in the New World in 1493, the dominant indigenous culture was that of the Taíno. The Taíno people's numbers went dangerously low during the later half of the 16th century because of new infectious diseases, other exploitation by Spanish settlers, and warfare.

Anguilla.lead: Anguilla is a British Overseas Territory of the Caribbean region in the North Atlantic Ocean. It is one of the most northerly of the Leeward Islands in the Lesser Antilles, lying east of Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands and directly north of Saint Martin.

Politics of Anguilla.lead: Politics of Anguilla takes place in a framework of a parliamentary representative democratic dependency, whereby the Premier is the head of government, and of a multi-party system. Anguilla, the most northerly of the Leeward Islands in the Lesser Antilles, is an internally self-governing overseas territory of the United Kingdom.

Elections in Anguilla.lead: Anguilla elects on territorial level a legislature. The House of Assembly has 13 members, 7 members elected for a five-year term in single-seat constituencies, 4 members elected at large and 2 ex officio members. Anguilla has a multi-party system.

History of Anguilla.lead: The history of Anguilla runs from the beginning of human habitation, probably via settlement from South America. Following a series of rebellions against white occupiers and a short-lived period as an independent republic during the 1960s, Anguilla has been a separate British overseas territory since 1980.

British Virgin Islands.lead: The British Virgin Islands, officially the Virgin Islands, is a British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean, to the east of Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands and north-west of Anguilla. The islands are geographically part of the Virgin Islands archipelago and are located in the Leeward Islands of the Lesser Antilles and part of the West Indies.

Cayman Islands.lead: The Cayman Islands is a self-governing British Overseas Territory in the western Caribbean. With a population of over 90,000, it is the most populated of all the British Overseas Territories. The 264-square-kilometre territory comprises the three islands of Grand Cayman, Cayman Brac and Little Cayman, which are located south of Cuba and north-east of Honduras, between Jamaica and Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula.

Bermuda.lead: Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory in the North Atlantic Ocean. The closest land outside the territory is in the US state of North Carolina, about 1,035 km to the west-northwest. Bermuda is an archipelago consisting of 181 islands, although the most significant islands are connected by bridges and appear to form one landmass. It has a land area of 54 square kilometres.

Politics of Bermuda.lead: Bermuda is the oldest British Overseas Territory, and the oldest self-governing British Overseas Territory, and has a great degree of internal autonomy through authority and roles of governance delegated to it by the national Government. Its parliament held its first session in 1620, making it the third-oldest continuous parliament in the world.

Elections in Bermuda.lead: Elections in Bermuda have been taking place since 1620. Bermuda's current electoral system, with a lower house elected by all Bermudian status-holders, each casting a single vote, voting in single-member districts on the first-past-the-post method, came into effect with the 1968 constitution.

History of Bermuda.lead: The recorded history of Bermuda dates back to 1503, when it was written about by the Spanish explorer Juan de Bermúdez, whose surname was used as the island's namesake.

Heard Island and McDonald Islands.lead: The Territory of Heard Island and McDonald Islands is an Australian external territory in the southern Indian Ocean. Discovered in the mid-19th century, the territory is a group of sub-Antarctic volcanic islands that lie on the Kerguelen Plateau. It is about 4000 kilometres south-west of the Australian mainland and 1700 kilometres north of Antarctica.

Government of Montana.lead: As established and defined by the Montana Constitution, the government of the State of Montana is composed of three branches, the Executive, Judicial, and Legislative. The powers of initiative and referendum are reserved for the citizens of Montana. The second and current state constitution was enacted in 1972.

Politics of Nebraska.stands: Nebraska is run by a group of elected senators, called ‘senators’, who meet in a building called the Unicameral. They make the laws for the state. The state’s government is divided into three parts: the people in charge, the lawmakers, and the judges.
Politics of Nebraska.lead: Nebraska is a landlocked state in the Great Plains and Midwestern region of the United States. It borders South Dakota to the north; Wyoming to the west; Colorado to the southwest; Kansas to the south; and Missouri to the southeast and Iowa to the east, both across the Missouri River. Nebraska is the 16th-largest state by land area, with just over 77,347 square miles.

Government of Nebraska.lead: S. State of Nebraska, established by the Nebraska Constitution, is a republican democracy modeled after the Federal Government of the United States. The state government has three branches: the executive, the legislative, and the judicial.

Politics of Nevada.lead: Nevada is a landlocked state in the Western United States. It is also sometimes placed in the Mountain West and Southwestern United States. It borders Idaho to the northeast, Oregon to the northwest, California to the west, Arizona to the southeast, and Utah to the east. S. state. Nearly three-quarters of Nevada's population live in Clark County, which contains the Las Vegas–Paradise metropolitan area.

Government of Nevada.lead: The government of Nevada is organized under the Constitution of Nevada of 1864 and divided into three branches of government. The executive branch consists of six independently elected officers, including the governor, lieutenant governor, secretary of state, attorney general, treasurer, and controller.

Politics of New Hampshire.lead: New Hampshire is often noted for its moderate politics and its status as a prominent swing state. The state's politics is also often considered libertarian-leaning, combining fiscal conservatism and social liberalism. Voters predominantly selected Republicans for national office during the 19th and 20th centuries until 1992. Since then, the state has been considered a swing state.

Government of New Hampshire.lead: The State of New Hampshire has a republican form of government modeled after the Government of the United States, with three branches: the executive, consisting of the Governor of New Hampshire, the elected Executive Council, and subordinate agencies; the legislative, called the New Hampshire General Court, which includes the Senate and the House of Representatives; and the judicial, consisting of the Supreme Court of New Hampshire and lower courts.

Politics of New Jersey.lead: S. state. The state is considered a stronghold of the Democratic Party and has supported the Democratic candidate in every presidential election since 1992. Democrats have also controlled both chambers of the state legislature since 2004. New Jersey currently has two Democratic United States senators. New Jersey's Class I Senate seat has been Democratic since 1959.

Government of New Jersey.lead: The government of the State of New Jersey is separated into three distinct branches: legislative, executive, and judicial. The powers of the State of New Jersey are vested by the Constitution of New Jersey, enacted in 1947, in a bicameral state legislature, the Governor, and the state courts, headed the New Jersey Supreme Court.

Politics of New Mexico.stands: The people of New Mexico vote to make the rules for their state. The governor and other important leaders are chosen by people voting for them, and the lawmakers (people who make the laws) are also chosen by voting. The lawmakers get paid very little while they're working, which is different from most other states.
Politics of New Mexico.lead: New Mexico is a landlocked state in the Southwestern region of the United States. It is one of the Mountain States of the southern Rocky Mountains, sharing the Four Corners region with Utah, Colorado, and Arizona. It also borders the state of Texas to the east and southeast, Oklahoma to the northeast, and shares an international border with the Mexican states of Chihuahua and Sonora to the south.

Government of New Mexico.lead: The government of New Mexico is the governmental structure of the state of New Mexico as established by the Constitution of New Mexico. The executive is composed of the governor, several other statewide elected officials and the governor's cabinet. The New Mexico Legislature consists of the House of Representatives and Senate. The judiciary is composed of the New Mexico Supreme Court and lower courts.

Politics of North Carolina.stands: The people of North Carolina choose their leaders by voting in elections for representatives in the U.S. House and Senate. The Governor is also chosen by the people, but the state has mostly elected Democratic governors throughout its history.
Politics of North Carolina.lead: S. states, North Carolina is politically dominated by the Democratic and Republican political parties, though the Republican Party holds an edge. S. S. Senate. North Carolina has voted for the Republican candidate in all but one presidential election since 1980; the one exception was in 2008, when a plurality of North Carolinians voted for Barack Obama.

Government of North Carolina.lead: The government of North Carolina is divided into three branches: executive, legislative, and judicial. These consist of the Council of State, the bicameral legislature, and the state court system. The Constitution of North Carolina delineates the structure and function of the state government.

Politics of North Dakota.stands: The Governor leads the state, and lawmakers are chosen by people voting in districts. The state has two groups of lawmakers – a Senate with 47 members and a House of Representatives with 94 members, both serving four-year terms.
Politics of North Dakota.lead: The politics of North Dakota were shaped historically by early settlement by people from the Northern Tier, who carried their politics west ultimately from New England, upstate New York, and the Upper Midwest. The area and state also received numerous European immigrants and migrants, particularly during the era of opening up of former Native American lands for sale and settlement.

Government of North Dakota.lead: S. state in the Upper Midwest, named after the indigenous Dakota and Sioux peoples. S. states of Minnesota to the east, South Dakota to the south, and Montana to the west. North Dakota is part of the Great Plains region, characterized by broad prairies, steppe, temperate savanna, badlands, and farmland.

Politics of Ohio.stands: The governor, Mike DeWine, leads Ohio, and all other top government leaders are Republicans. The state legislature, both the Senate and the House, is controlled by the Republican party, with a large majority of seats.
